scenario.title: First Battle of Grammos
intro.text:
FIRST BATTLE OF GRAMMOS - 18 JUL 1948

Mt Grammos, Pindus Mountains

The battle for the Grammos mountains raged for nearly a month and the Athenian fascists send more and more mercenary troops into battle. We have no choice, we must abandon the Grammos mountains temporarily and dare the breakout! To achieve this, you will carry out a concentrated attack on the center of the enemy forces! Beat a breach in the enemy's ranks and lead our troops in Northeast direction to the Vitsi mountains!

GOAL Retreat 9 ground units via Exit Points!
header.act: ACT IV — THE WAR IN THE MOUNTAINS
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-25-0-briliant.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.reaction-25-0-briliant.text: Konitsa is ours. I can announce that the Provisional Government holds its town. Recognition has still not come, and we need a supply route before the National Army returns.
line.reaction-25-1-victory-tactical.text: The town objectives were taken after a costly fight. Government forces are regrouping outside the area, and holding Konitsa may demand more army than taking it did.
line.reaction-25-2-lose.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.reaction-25-2-lose.text: We couldn't take Konitsa. The men are coming back from the approaches. Ask them what happened before issuing another order to find a capital.
line.callback-0.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.callback-0.text: The Party is asking which territory we can govern after Konitsa. I know recognition hasn't followed. I still need something more to put before foreign governments than another account of our marches.
line.callback-1.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.callback-1.text: The formations we kept outside Konitsa are available here. Party headquarters is still asking why we didn't take the town. I'll answer again if it keeps these units free to move.
line.earned-decision.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.earned-decision.text: The Konitsa mortar group carried its tubes, tables, and wounded observers out together. It can serve Grammos as a battery, or feed crews and bombs to rifle units already asking for both.
line.earned-decision.choice.keep-konitsa: Keep the Konitsa mortar group as a separate battery.
Add an experienced seven-strength 81 mm mortar unit.
line.earned-decision.choice.spread-konit: Distribute the mortar crews and ammunition through the core.
Give infantry 15 experience and fully rearm the core.
line.earned-a-response.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.earned-a-response.text: Keep the battery. Its observers and crews brought their equipment out together. I want them working with the same people when we register the Grammos positions.
line.earned-b-response.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.earned-b-response.text: Send the crews and ammunition to the rifle battalions. Tell the battery commander where his observers go; they can still coordinate their work from different units.
line.scene-0.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.scene-0.text: Families below Nestorio are being taken out of their villages and held behind wire. Our messengers can't find their contacts. We are losing food, guides and recruits along with those homes.
line.scene-1.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.scene-1.text: Without the villages, where do you expect us to get food and information? Keep us on the ridges and the aircraft can work over the same positions every day.
line.scene-2.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.scene-2.text: And an army which abandons every liberated district saves Athens the trouble of admitting there is another authority in Greece.
line.scene-3.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-3.text: The western hospital has twelve mules for thirty-one stretchers. Before anyone says 'hold' or 'withdraw,' I would like to know which nineteen wounded are part of the political argument.
line.decision.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.decision.text: Commander: build the artillery front and hold Grammos, or prepare the western corridors while there is still time to move an army through them?
line.decision.choice.hold-the-grammos-fr: Build a fixed artillery front and hold Grammos as liberated territory.
Give infantry and artillery 20 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition.
line.decision.choice.prepare-the-corrido: Prepare three withdrawal corridors, caches, and a mobile rear guard.
Give reconnaissance 20 experience, fully refuel and rearm the core, and set aside transport for the wounded.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.choice-a-0.text: Then give the local commanders authority to pull a company off a lost ridge. If every request has to reach headquarters first, some won't arrive until the men are gone.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.choice-a-1.text: Local withdrawals require approval. Register the guns, deepen the shelters, and make Grammos a front the government must attack openly.
line.choice-a-2.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-2.text: I'll move the spare mules to the hospital. If we are staying, the wounded need a road even when the battalions do not.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.choice-b-0.text: The villages will hear 'corridors' and understand retreat. Once that word spreads, it moves faster than your rear guard.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.choice-b-1.text: Tell the villages before the last battalion leaves. Three routes, caches and closing hours. Withdraw the guns while their crews can still move them; don't wait until we have to abandon both.
